items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: my cousin Harold and Lettego and a banjo player named Birdie and a base player named Fletcher, they all used to play all the house parties around there.

ctx.x: Well, there was a guy in Miami, his last name was Abrista, but one night a couple of guys got in a fight, and he was from the Bahamas and he was telling the guys to let him go, but instead of saying let him go, he said, "lette go", and he got this nickname, "Lettego", and everybody used to call him Lettego and so he and my cousin Harold who was a trumpet player, and he used to play all the house parties around Miami.

And my father was a bootlegger, and like every one once a month, he would have a party at the house so he could sell his liquor, and my cousin Harold and Lettego and a banjo player named Birdie and a base player named Fletcher, they all used to play all the house parties around there.
In fact, that's when I first saw a Coca Cola bottle being used as a mute. I think I was about 6 or 7 years old at the time, but I remember it well.
